aj-ayer.oneLineEn: Language, Truth and Logic brought the Vienna Circle into the English-speaking world.

alain-locke.oneLineEn: Philosophical interpreter of the Harlem Renaissance; argued value pluralism across cultural difference.

alexandre-kojeve.oneLineEn: Lectures on the Phenomenology via master-slave dialectic shaped a generation of French thinkers.

alexius-meinong.oneLineEn: Founder of the theory of objects; non-existent objects still have a way of being, shaping ontology debates.

alvin-plantinga.oneLineEn: Reformed epistemology and modal ontological argument; theistic belief can be properly basic.

bachelard.oneLineEn: Recast history of science through epistemological break and obstacle, plus a poetics of material imagination.

badiou.oneLineEn: Being and Event builds ontology and an evental conception of truth on set theory.

baudrillard.oneLineEn: Analyzed consumer society's symbolic logic through simulacra and hyperreality.

bourdieu.oneLineEn: Built a theory of social practice around habitus, field, and cultural capital.

bruno-latour.oneLineEn: Actor-network theory brings nonhumans into social analysis.

brunschvicg.oneLineEn: Hub of French academic epistemology via philosophy of judgment and history of the scientific spirit.

canguilhem.oneLineEn: The Normal and the Pathological rewrote philosophy of medicine via vital normativity; Foucault's mentor.

cavailles.oneLineEn: Opposed philosophy of consciousness with a philosophy of the concept; executed for Resistance activity.

cd-broad.oneLineEn: Cambridge synthesizer of mind, ethics, and metaphysics, known for fine classification and moderate eclecticism.

ci-lewis.oneLineEn: Conceptual pragmatism and modal logic; strict implication answered material-implication paradoxes.

claude-lefort.oneLineEn: Defined democracy by the empty place of power and systematically critiqued totalitarianism.

cornelius-castoriadis.oneLineEn: Social imaginary institution and autonomy theory as a heterodox Western Marxism.

cournot.oneLineEn: Linked positivism and French epistemology via probability, economics, and theories of chance.

david-armstrong.oneLineEn: Australian materialist whose realist universals and mind-brain identity form a metaphysical system.

duhem.oneLineEn: Duhem thesis: hypotheses cannot be tested in isolation; paved the way for Quinean holism.

emmanuel-mounier.oneLineEn: Founder of the personalist movement; launched Esprit for personhood and community.

eric-voegelin.oneLineEn: Diagnosed modernity through political religion and philosophy of order, treating Gnosticism as the disease.

ernst-cassirer.oneLineEn: Founder of the philosophy of symbolic forms, uniting myth, language, and science as human symbolization.

ernst-troeltsch.oneLineEn: Historicism and philosophy of religion at the crossroads of Dilthey, Weber, and theological modernity.

etienne-gilson.oneLineEn: Reread Aquinas around esse and advanced the historiography of medieval philosophy.

fh-bradley.oneLineEn: British absolute idealist; internal relations became a main target of the Russell-Moore revolt.

frank-ramsey.oneLineEn: Early hub of truth, probability, decision, and economics; foundational work despite death at twenty-six.

franz-brentano.oneLineEn: Revived intentionality; descriptive psychology linked Aristotle, scholasticism, and Husserl.

gabriel-marcel.oneLineEn: Christian existentialist who distinguished mystery from problem and developed a phenomenology of hope.

georg-simmel.oneLineEn: Formal sociology and cultural philosophy analyzing modern experience via interaction forms and money.
